subject: financial_literacy
concept: Understanding cash flow: the timing difference between when money comes in and when it must go out, and why a profitable business can still run into trouble
source_inspiration: original content — not sourced from any external text

exercise.concrete: Student tracks a simple month-by-month cash flow for a small business, noting when expenses come due before revenue arrives
exercise.pictorial: Student matches a cash flow timing gap to the risk it creates for the business
exercise.abstract: Student explains why a business can be profitable overall but still run short on cash at a specific point in time

misconception_flags: confuses overall profitability with having enough cash on hand at any given moment

interest_binding: exercise regenerated using student's stated interest profile
